readingReview.comparison: The first reader's natural order is the intended order in every panel: 05-1 [1, 2], 05-2 [1, 2, 3], 05-3 [1, 2], 05-4 [1]. Each concern was checked. Acceptable: the reader chose the balloon because it is 184 px higher, which is the intended order, and in the art the label sits over the foreground laptop screen while the balloon's tail is at Ananya's mouth. (2) A reply to Ravi might be skipped. Acceptable: 'I've been feeling tired lately.' answers the 05-1 'Tell me what brings you in.', and the consent exchange that comes between them is the user's explicit 2026-11-12 requirement (consent before any voice is saved). Ananya responds non-verbally in 05-4 (art: leaning in, folded hands, nod marks, eye contact), and verbally in 06-2 with 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together', which picks up 'tired'. Source PAGE 5 has the same structure. (3) The two balloons in 05-2 touch and the tail is crowded. Acceptable: the tails split to the two speakers at opposite ends, and the 'Yes, I agree.' tail now visibly clears the consent label corner by about 5-8 px in both storyboard PNGs and the preview. (4) The consent label is read after the agreement. Acceptable: it is screen content naming the step that just happened, and the dialogue itself already shows asking before recording. (5) Text touches the panel frames. Acceptable for this stage: the text keeps its inner padding and is legible in the preview, and I noted it for lettering polish. (6) Ravi appears in 05-4 only as a dot. Resolved: the accepted art shows the back of his head and shoulder at the lower right. (7) The text is dense. Acceptable: the user asked for the full wording ('add page if needed'), and the screen walk-through was split across pages 5 and 6 to make room. Nothing is unresolved.
